review.problem: The black book rests on the flat blue target, whose pickup edge needs more frontward exposure.
review.rationale: Stand and relocate the black book first so it no longer loads the target; then prepare the blue book for its own pickup.
review.notes: Task and robot contexts are authored scenario assumptions, not observed robot logs. All three unchanged photographs were visually reviewed; only image 01 is supplied to the VLM. On 2026-10-27 the collector authorized reuse of existing numeric candidate distances as measured or deliberately staged. Legacy T007. The collector specified upright black 90-degree clockwise turn, 10 cm right with the blue book as reference, then blue 3 cm forward. Here forward is interpreted as forward out of the shelf toward its open edge, consistent with the immediately preceding edge-grasp question and the prior toward-camera instructions; the composer encodes that physical direction as backward, not away-from-camera forward. The collector confirmed these distances are displacements from the moved book, while the named reference supplies directional context. Accordingly the move uses direction plus reference_object, not placement. The current composer accepts that combination; its displacement planner uses the frozen captured axes, rather than calculating a destination from the reference anchor. REVIEW BEFORE SFT: image-plane rotations use captured Z and from_negative_axis, the camera-facing side of the frozen heading frame. Clockwise therefore compiles to a negative signed Z angle; counterclockwise compiles to a positive signed Z angle. The collector supplied the angles and intended end states. Actual 3D pose and grounding-anchor offsets were not measured. The upright-book pivot is an idealized geometry construction, assuming a body-midpoint anchor, 22 cm spine length along captured X, 4 cm flat thickness and a level shelf. S0031 top/middle stack support heights are 8/4 cm; S0033 black-book support is the measured 6 cm blue-book thickness. These derive from the original measured book dimensions, not measured capture poses. Under this model the turn also shifts the center 13 cm right and brings the final upright bottom to the shelf plane. The requested 10/5 cm rightward move is additional to that turning motion. Physical clearance, shelf support, actual book orientation and grounded anchor must be checked before SFT; constraints are descriptive, not collision checks.
